bib.title: Reasoning on Graphs: Faithful and Interpretable Large Language Model Reasoning

SOURCE: "Reasoning on Graphs: Faithful and Interpretable Large Language Model Reasoning", Linhao Luo, Yuan-Fang Li, Gholamreza Haffari (Monash), Shirui Pan (Griffith). ICLR 2024 (arXiv:2310.01061v2, 24 Feb 2024). File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/ai-engineering/05-graph-engineering/sources/luo-2023-reasoning-graphs.pdf

COVERAGE: 24 of 24 pages read; about 79,700 of 82,191 extracted chars. I read the whole body, Appendix A.1 to A.10 (all results tables, prompts, Algorithm 1, case studies) and most of the references. I skipped about 2.5k chars (offsets roughly 41,500 to 44,000), and they are reference-list entries only (part of L through S). There is no separate limitations section.

CLAIMS
- claim: RoG is a planning-retrieval-reasoning framework. The LLM generates relation paths (sequences of KG relations) as plans. Those paths are executed on the KG to retrieve concrete reasoning paths, and the LLM answers from those paths with an explanation.
  number: none
  setup: method; one LLM does both planning and reasoning
  quote: "RoG first generates relation paths grounded by KGs as faithful plans. These plans are then used to retrieve valid reasoning paths from the KGs for LLMs to conduct faithful reasoning."
  where: abstract, p1
- claim: The plans are relation paths rather than entities because relations change less often than entities, so the same plan keeps retrieving current facts.
  number: none
  setup: design argument, not measured
  quote: "compared to the dynamically updated entities, the relations in KGs are more stable (Wang et al., 2023a). By using relation paths, we can always retrieve the latest knowledge from KGs for reasoning."
  where: p4, sec 4.1
- claim: Training uses two instruction-tuning tasks derived from an ELBO. Planning is supervised by the shortest KG paths between question and answer entities. Retrieval-reasoning trains the model to answer from retrieved paths, using FiD-style aggregation.
  number: none
  setup: shortest paths Z* used as supervision signals (credited to Zhang et al., 2022)
  quote: "we use the shortest paths Z ∗ ⊆ Zbetween eq and ea in KGs as supervision signals (Zhang et al., 2022)"
  where: p5, eq 4
- claim: Retrieval is a constrained breadth-first search. It starts from the question entities and follows each relation in the plan in order. All retrieved paths go to the reasoner.
  number: none
  setup: Algorithm 1, Appendix A.3
  quote: "We adopt a constrained breadth-first search to retrieve the reasoning paths wz from KGs. In experiments, all retrieved paths are used for reasoning."
  where: p6
- claim: Headline result: RoG beats 21 baselines on Hits@1 on both datasets, with relative gains of 4.4% over DECAF on WebQSP and 22.3% (Hits@1) and 14.4% (F1) over UniKGQA on CWQ.
  number: WebQSP Hits@1 85.7 / F1 70.8; CWQ Hits@1 62.6 / F1 56.2
  setup: LLaMA2-Chat-7B fine-tuned for 3 epochs on WebQSP and CWQ train splits plus Freebase; top-3 relation paths by beam search. Baseline figures are copied from the UniKGQA and DECAF papers. The percentages are relative gains (85.7/82.1 = 1.044).
  quote: "compared to the SOTA method DECAF (Yu et al., 2022a) on WebQSP, our method improves Hits@1 by 4.4%. On the CWQ dataset, which is more challenging due to multi-hop questions, our method improves both Hits@1 and F1 by 22.3% and 14.4% against the SOTA model UniKGQA"; Table 1 row "RoG 85.7 70.8 62.6 56.2"
  where: p7, Table 1, sec 5.2
- claim: Baseline rows from Table 1, for context. RoG does NOT have the best WebQSP F1: DECAF, RnG-KBQA, ArcaneQA, QGG and UniKGQA all score higher.
  number: DECAF 82.1/78.8; UniKGQA 77.2/72.2 and 51.2/49.1; ChatGPT 66.8 and 39.9; ChatGPT+CoT 75.6 and 48.9; RnG-KBQA F1 76.2
  setup: WebQSP Hits@1/F1, CWQ Hits@1/F1

  where: p7, Table 1
- claim: Plug-and-play. The RoG planner's retrieved paths, given to other LLMs without retraining, improve every one of them.
  number: ChatGPT 66.77 to 81.51 Hits@1 (WebQSP), 39.90 to 52.68 (CWQ); Flan-T5-xl 30.95 to 67.87 (WebQSP)

LIMITS
- There is no limitations section. "Faithful" is never measured as explanation fidelity. The evidence is answer coverage of retrieved paths plus hand-picked cases.
- Some of the paper's own cases undercut the faithfulness claim. In Table 20 (Walt Disney), the explanation infers "child" from a path that reads "Walt Disney → people.person.parents → Sharon Mae Disney". In the Louisiana case, the explanation asserts "The United States of America is in the Central Time Zone."
- Entities in the question and the answers are assumed to be labeled and linked to the KG, i.e. gold entity linking: "we assume the entities eq ∈ Tq mentioned in q and answers a ∈ Aq are labeled and linked".
- The KG is a Freebase subgraph of entities within the max hop count of the question entities (2,566,291 entities, 8,309,195 triples). The body text cites full Freebase at 88M entities.
- Baseline numbers are copied from other papers rather than re-run. The LLM baselines are zero-shot, while RoG is fine-tuned (Table 16 partly addresses this). RoG trains on WebQSP+CWQ together, while UniKGQA trains on one dataset.
- Results cover only 7B LLaMA2-Chat and July to Sept 2023 ChatGPT. Max hops are 2 (WebQSP) and 4 (CWQ).
- WebQSP F1 (70.8) trails the semantic-parsing methods and DECAF.
- The planner needs KG-specific fine-tuning, because "the LLMs have zero knowledge of the relations contained in KGs".
- The 2,000 explanation-training instances were generated by ChatGPT.

BUILDS ON: plan-and-solve (Wang et al., 2023c); FiD (Izacard & Grave, 2021; Singh et al., 2021); relation-path subgraph retrieval and shortest-path supervision, SR+NSM (Zhang et al., 2022); ELBO / variational methods (Jordan et al., 1999); UniKGQA (Jiang et al., 2022); DECAF (Yu et al., 2022a); KD-CoT (Wang et al., 2023b); RR (He et al., 2022); ReAct (Yao et al., 2022); CoT (Wei et al., 2022); Freebase (Bollacker et al., 2008); WebQSP (Yih et al., 2016); CWQ (Talmor & Berant, 2018). Related work also cites Think-on-Graph (Sun et al., 2024) and KG-Agent (Jiang et al., 2024). Code: https://github.com/RManLuo/reasoning-on-graphs

CODE
- Planning prompt (p5, p22): "Please generate a valid relation path that can be helpful for answering the following question: <Question>". Output format: "z = <PATH> r1 <SEP> r2 <SEP> . . .<SEP> rl </PATH>"
- Reasoning prompt (p22): "Based on the reasoning paths, please answer the given question. Please keep the answer as simple as possible and return all the possible answers as a list. Reasoning Paths: <Reasoning Paths> Question: <Question>"
- Algorithm 1 (p17), the constrained BFS. Its core step: "r ← z[len(wz) + 1]; // Get relation for next step. foreach (s, r′, t) ∈ Gdo if r′ = r then w′z.append((s, r, t)); Q.append((t, w′z));"
- Objective (p5, eq 7): L = log Pθ(a|q, Z*K, G) [retrieval-reasoning] + 1/|Z*| Σ log Pθ(z|q) [planning]
- Table 19 (p23) shows example generated relation paths, e.g. "sports.mascot.team → sports.sports team.arena stadium".

FIGURES
- Figure 2, p3: "The overall framework of reasoning on graphs (RoG)..." It shows planning, retrieval and reasoning on one KG example (Joe Biden nationality). This is the best single picture of the pipeline for the KG-RAG note.
- Figure 1, p2: it contrasts lack of knowledge and hallucination, and shows a triple vs a relation path as the fix. It makes "relation path as plan" clear quickly.
- Figure 3, p8: as top-K grows, retrieved paths and answer coverage rise while reasoning F1 stays flat. It shows the recall/noise trade-off visually.
- Figure 4, p21: retrieval time and path count against K. Minor.
- Tables 4 and 5 (p9) work well as side-by-side examples of ChatGPT+CoT vs RoG.

PROBLEMS
- Prose and table disagree on the plug-and-play gains. The text says "the Hits@1 of ChatGPT, Alpaca, LLaMA2, and Flan-T5 are improved by 8.5%, 15.3%, and 119.3%, respectively": four models, three numbers. From Table 3, 8.5% is Alpaca, 15.3% is LLaMA2 and 119.3% is Flan-T5; ChatGPT's own gain (+22%) is missing from the prose. Cite Table 3, not the sentence.
- The Table 3 Alpaca + RoG row ("56.16 74.20") looks like the LLaMA2 + RoG Hits@1/Recall values ("74.20 56.16") swapped. It may be a typo in the paper; treat with caution.
- Table 14 prints "72,2" for UniKGQA F1, a typo for 72.2.
- Math and figure text extract with broken spacing and arrows. All the numbers above came through cleanly.
- No embedded instructions found.
